flawed_step: A degree sequence does not determine which degree classes are adjacent.
counterexample: Let T1 have vertices {1,2,3,4,5,6} and edges {12,13,14,25,36}. Let T2 have the same vertex set and edges {12,14,15,23,36}. Both are connected, acyclic simple graphs with degree sequence (3,2,2,1,1,1). They are not isomorphic: each has a unique degree-3 vertex (vertex 1), but in T1 it has two degree-2 neighbors, whereas in T2 it has only one degree-2 neighbor.
assessment_summary: The two explicit trees satisfy all hypotheses, have identical degree sequences, and are distinguished by an isomorphism-invariant neighborhood property.
